title: the left operand of a comma expression discards the Result it produced
notes: specification/failures.mdx:136: 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' specification/type-system.mdx:56: 'An ignored Result MUST be a compile error.' Only the right operand of a comma becomes the expression's value; the left one is evaluated and dropped. REVIEW-fable-1.md F1 measured this exact program COMPILING, EMITTING AND RUNNING on the Go fork with zero diagnostics: the checked value was discarded at runtime, which is the loss the rule exists to prevent. The fork's unbound must-consume rule fired only when an expression statement's own expression typed as Result or Promise, so every container and operator position was invisible to it. The comma is also the reason the fork's rule missed a whole family: it returned early on every binary expression on the theory that a binary expression is an assignment, and comma, `&&` and `||` are binary expressions too. 07-must-consume/an-ownership-transfer-in-every-position-is-accepted holds the other side, where the comma's value IS used.
